claim: Client-side under-payment spans three architectural dimensions: state synchronization (B0), commitment timing (M1), usage authority (M2).
Each mechanism localizes to a distinct state transition (AUTHORIZED->RESERVED; STREAMING->ABORTED; ACCOUNTED->RECONCILED).
B0 leakage is created by concurrency: zero at c=1, linear thereafter (slope 0.099/request, R^2=1.0000, p=1.9e-50).
Hardened atomic compare-and-decrement leaks $0 at every tested concurrency.
M1 leakage rises monotonically with abort position and collapses to zero at completion.
metric: mean leak per request vs abort_bin

claim: M1 per-request leakage is invariant to concurrency (identical to 4 dp across c=1..100 with request volume held constant).
Honest clients (no abort) leak zero on every architecture.
Client-authoritative billing leaks; server-authoritative billing leaks zero for every manipulation tested.
Which manipulation succeeds depends on the pricing basis: total/subtotal mismatch is inert under category pricing (0.000) but the strongest attack under flat-total pricing (0.741).
M2 leakage efficiency is invariant to concurrency.
Abort-inclusive finalization closes M1's integrity violation with or without a reservation.
Reservation independently provides solvency: without it the balance goes negative under a constrained budget.
Performing a recount is insufficient: client_logged computes an authoritative recount and still leaks (efficiency 0.595) because billing ignores it.
Tokenizer recount cost is linear in input length (log-log slope 0.999-1.14, R^2>=0.998).
metric: log-log regression of p50 latency vs tokens

claim: Tokenizer engine choice changes recount cost by ~2.9-3.6x at 16384 tokens.
With a mock (zero-cost) generator, gateway recount costs up to 95% of throughput at 16384 tokens; tokenization time explains it (Spearman rho=-0.868, p=1.3e-5).
With real local inference, the recount is 0.012-0.016% of end-to-end time at every context size.
The apparent expense of recount under the mock gateway is an artifact of the generator costing nothing.
metric: comparison of mock-gateway vs real-model ratios

claim: Integrity gates fail closed: six corruption types are each detected for both M1 and M2 (12/12).
An independently coded checker agrees with the gateway on all cross-validated cells (42 M2, 16 M1, 2 B0).
Hardened architectures survive nine injected lifecycle failures; recount-engine failure is fail-closed.
Leakage efficiency is invariant under uniform price scaling (low->medium x10) and shifts by at most ~0.012 under a price-structure change.
Flat-total pricing systematically overcharges honest clients (negative leak).
Logging a server recount moves an M2 leak from D0 (invisible) to D1 (reconcilable) without preventing it.
Prior LLM-billing security work covers provider over-charge, victim bill inflation, and intermediary provenance; not client under-payment.
M1 and M2 are type-B systematization contributions, not novel primitives; B0 is a known baseline.
Results do NOT generalize to commercial providers or production serving stacks.
